_readme: Closes every remaining gap, including chapter intros and discussion sections. For discussion-style sections (1.2, 10.2, 10.4) the question checks comprehension of the section's own framing rather than asking for a personal opinion, since opinions can't be graded right/wrong.

quizzes.question: Who — or what — is ShalaKasi, as introduced in this section?
options: A real teacher who visits in person once a week
An AI mentor built into the platform, here to guide you through the Diploma
A textbook chapter title

quizzes.question: What does ShalaKasi say it will help with throughout the Diploma?
options: Explaining ideas differently when something doesn't click, and tracking where you're strong or need another pass
Grading attendance only
Replacing Sassa and Bongani entirely

quizzes.question: What is the actual goal of this class discussion, according to the section itself?
options: To reach one single correct answer everyone must agree on
To notice that money is stranger and more designed than it first appears
To memorize a list of definitions

quizzes.question: What question does this section say we're going 'one level deeper' into, compared to Chapter 1?
options: Why money is necessary
What money actually is
How to mine Bitcoin

quizzes.question: What is this chapter's overall path, as described in the introduction?
options: From direct trade between people, all the way to the card or app you use now
From Bitcoin back to gold
From mining to spending, skipping history entirely

quizzes.question: What does the word 'fiat' mean, as explained in this section?
options: A type of car
Roughly 'let it be done' in Latin — a decree
A synonym for gold

quizzes.question: According to this section, where do the effects of the fiat system actually show up?
options: Only in economics textbooks, not real life
In everyday things like a rising taxi fare or a stokvel payout buying less than before
Nowhere — the effects are purely theoretical

quizzes.question: What does this chapter promise you'll actually do, not just read about?
options: Mine a Bitcoin block
Set up a wallet and send a real transaction
Write Bitcoin's source code

quizzes.question: Why was the Lightning Network built on top of Bitcoin, according to this section?
options: To replace Bitcoin entirely
To make small, fast, cheap everyday payments practical, since the base blockchain is slower and costlier for that
To make Bitcoin more expensive to use

quizzes.question: What does this section say Lightning's speed and low fees make practical?
options: Only large business-to-business transfers
Genuine everyday spending, like buying coffee or groceries
Nothing new compared to the base blockchain

quizzes.question: Does this chapter require you to become a programmer, according to its introduction?
options: Yes, coding is required to continue
No — but understanding the mechanics makes you a more confident, self-sufficient user
Only if you plan to become a miner

quizzes.question: What bigger question has the whole Diploma been building toward, according to this closing chapter's introduction?
options: Why any of this actually matters for your own life
How to write a Bitcoin whitepaper
Which wallet brand is the best

quizzes.question: According to this section, what does Bitcoin do to the real tensions around control of money (privacy vs. crime-fighting, control vs. safety nets)?
options: It fully resolves all of them
It shifts who is responsible for navigating them, rather than resolving them
It has no effect on these tensions at all

quizzes.question: According to this closing section, what was the actual outcome this Diploma was built to create?
options: Memorizing Bitcoin's full source code
A shift in perspective — understanding money could be different, with the tools to participate in that difference
Passing a final written exam
